newsitem.title: USA: Nuveen taps Wilscheetz for muni banking.
newsitem.headline: Nuveen taps Wilscheetz for muni banking.

text.p: John Nuveen & Co has hired former Cambridge Partners LLC municipal bond professional Tim Wilscheetz as part of a drive to beef up Nuveen's Investment Banking Division.

"What is new at Nuveen--I guess it's somewhat counter cyclical in the industry--is that we made a judgement roughly a year ago to add significantly to our investment banking staff, " said Clifton Fenton, manager of Nuveen's Investment Banking Divison.

While the traditional investment banking business does not justify large-scale staff increases, Nuveen took a look at its client base, and concluded some business opportunities lay ahead. The firm decided it could benefit from those opportunities by broadening its talent base, Fenton said. Nuveen specializes in education, health care, housing and utitlities, he said.

Nuveen believes that privatization is one area that offers opportunities going forward, and Wilscheetz experience in that area will be key, Fenton said. Wilscheetz was involved in privatization work during his 1-1/2 years at Cambridge, Fenton said.

"Tim's been involved in some interesting transactions over there that generally fit under the rubic of privatization," Fenton said. "Plus he's just a very talented guy, with the basic skills set that we look for at Nuveen."

Wilscheetz will be working in the transportation and utility sectors, and will participate in such traditional acitivities such as bond underwriting in addition to services that may revolve around privatization, Fenton said.
Wilscheetz said his work over the past year has evolved into what is referred to as "public-private partnership" transactions.
While such public-private partnerships continue to generate interest, growth in that sector hinges largely on external forces, he said.

"The trend is probably growing, the extent to which it takes place is dictated by things that are outside of our control to a larget extent, government regulation and other things," Wilscheetz said. "It's hard to tell exactly where it takes off."
Wilscheetz, who started at Nuveen January 13, was one of two recent hires, Fenton.
Mark Laubacher, who like Wilscheetz has joined Nuveen as a vice president in investment banking, began work at the firm in December, he said.

"We are coming close to completing the personnel complement that we want to have going forward," Fenton said, adding that Wilscheetz and Laubacher were two of about six or seven people that have joined the firm's investment banking division during the past year.
Excluding Wilscheetz, Nuveen Investment Banking had a total of 53 people in sales, trading, underwriting, and investment banking at year end 1996, Fenton said.
Prior to Cambrdige, Wilscheetz worked for approximately four years at Merrill Lynch & Co. He has a bachelor in engineering form Purdue University in 1983, and an MBA from Columbia University in 1991.
Wilscheetz will have offices in both New York and Chicago.
